Based on the pearly appearance of the bumps and the distinct central umbilication, I have identified the condition. It is a common viral skin infection in children that often resolves on its own.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum

dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me where on the body these skin lesions are located and when they first appeared?
They are mostly on my tummy and some on my arms and legs. My mommy noticed them a little while ago, but they don't really hurt or itch at all.
Thank you for sharing that. Could you describe what the spots look like, specifically their color and if they are flat or raised?
They are shiny and skin-colored, like little pearly bumps that stick up from my skin. If you look really closely at the middle of them, they have a tiny little dent or hole in the center.
Do you have a history of dry, itchy skin or eczema? Also, has anyone else in your family or at school had these same pearly bumps lately?
I don't have any itchy skin or eczema, and I feel pretty healthy. My mommy said another kid at my daycare had bumps like these, and my brother just got over the chickenpox last month.
I'm glad to hear you're feeling healthy otherwise. Have you had any fevers lately, and do the bumps ever get red, sore, or leak any fluid?
No, I haven't had any fevers at all. The bumps aren't red or sore, and nothing ever leaks out of them.
I'd like to take a closer look at these pearly bumps to be sure. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Examination
RESULTS: Multiple skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities; lesions are firm, without warmth or erythema.
